title: Baidu Open-Sources ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, Reshaping the Cost-Effectiveness Benchmark for Large-Parameter, Small-Activation Models with MoE Architecture

content_html:
In the field of open-source large models, developers are falling into a widespread kind of “parameter anxiety”: models are becoming more capable, but the accompanying high inference costs and huge VRAM usage are deterring many small and medium-sized teams. We urgently need a pragmatic solution that preserves “large-model intelligence” while also delivering “small-model speed.”

Recently, Baidu officially announced the open-sourcing of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, under the extremely permissive Apache 2.0 license, with model weights now fully available on Hugging Face and ModelScope. This is not just a routine model release; it is also a highly sincere engineering answer from Baidu to the industry pain point of “balancing inference cost and performance.”

 Architecture Breakthrough: 280 Billion Parameters, So Why Activate Only 14 Billion at a Time?

The core highlight of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is its deep optimization of the MoE (Mixture of Experts) architecture. The model has a total of 280 billion parameters, but when processing each token, it activates only 14 billion of them.

This design—“a very large brain capacity, but only specific brain regions are called on each time”—produces immediate results:

- Extreme inference speed: Official data shows that its generation speed can steadily exceed 200 tokens/sec, completely shattering the stereotype that ultra-large-parameter models “generate like snails.”

- Ultra-long context support: It natively supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens. Whether facing a complex codebase with millions of lines or hundreds of pages of industry research reports, it can read everything in one pass and pinpoint information accurately.

 Benchmark Data: A “Top Student” in Coding and Automation Scenarios

In officially published benchmarks, ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview shows a clear scenario orientation, performing impressively especially in the coding and business workflow automation areas that developers care about most:

- Code and Web development: On the CodeArena WebDev leaderboard, the model scored 1,668 points, ranking second among open-source models and fourth among domestic models. Its score is not only slightly higher than DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (1,664 points) and Kimi K3 (1,658 points), but also places it in the same tier as the industry benchmark Qwen3.8-Max (1,670 points).

- Agent automation: In the AutomationBench test, which focuses on business workflow automation, it scored as high as 61.9 points, even surpassing Claude Opus5.5 (58.0 points) and DeepSeek V4.1Flash1017 (57.2 points), proving its reliability in complex task orchestration.

Of course, the data also objectively reflects the model’s boundaries: in tests such as Terminal-Bench4.0 that place higher demands on extremely complex logic (score 46.5), it still has a gap compared with Claude Opus5.5 (63.6 points). But this precisely shows that Flash Preview’s positioning is very clear—it is not meant to be an all-powerful god, but the most efficient tool in specific scenarios.

 Ecosystem Significance: Making “Local Deployment” More Than Empty Talk

For developers, no matter how good a model is, if it is difficult to deploy, it is just a castle in the air. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview natively supports mainstream inference frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang, meaning developers can seamlessly integrate it into existing local or private cloud workflows for low-cost secondary development and fine-tuning.
